definitions.explanation: An area where people live, as opposed to wilderness or uninhabited mountain/forest areas. Often used when describing remote locations in relation to human settlements.

examples.japanese: {人里|ひとざと}⟦{離|はな}れた→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: I live in a place far from human habitation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{熊|くま}→熊：04343_kuma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{人里|ひとざと}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{下|お}りてきた。
examples.english: A bear came down to the inhabited area.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鹿|しか}→鹿：04347_shika⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べ{物|もの}→食べ物：02890_tabemono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{求|もと}めて→求める：02316_motomeru⟧{人里|ひとざと}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}づく→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In winter, deer sometimes approach human settlements in search of food.

notes:
USAGE:
{人里|ひとざと} is most commonly used in the expression {人里|ひとざと}⟦{離|はな}れた→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧ (far from human habitation), describing remote or secluded locations. It is also frequently used in nature and wildlife contexts when animals approach populated areas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人里|ひとざと}⟦{離|はな}れた→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧: remote, far from settlements
- {人里|ひとざと}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧: near inhabited areas
- {人里|ひとざと}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{下|お}りる: to come down to human settlements (of animals)
- {人里|ひとざと}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{遠|とお}い→遠い：00529_tooi⟧: far from inhabited areas
